title: India International Water Week 2026 Begins: Vice-President Asks Citizens to Save Every Drop
content:
## What Happened

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan launched the 9th India International Water Week 2026 on September 22. The event is being held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The Ministry of Jal Shakti is organising it for five days, from September 22 to 26. This year, the focus is on “Climate Resilient Water Management.”

At the event, the Vice-President launched two new tools. One is the Sustainable Urban River Management (SURM) Framework. The other is an AI and machine learning system for managing sediment in reservoirs. Union Minister for Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Patil and Ministers of State Shri V. Somanna and Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary were also present. Experts and delegates from India and other countries joined the programme.

## Why It Matters

India is home to about 18 per cent of the world's people. But it has only about 4 per cent of the world's freshwater. It also covers only about 2.4 per cent of the world's land area. This means every drop counts for you and for the country.

The Vice-President said water is the base of life and of civilisations. He shared that he grew up in Tamil Nadu and saw water scarcity himself. He asked citizens to change small daily habits. He said, “We can take a bath using two buckets or twenty buckets. The choice is ours.” He also reminded people to close the tap while brushing their teeth.

He said climate change, fast urban growth and a rising population are making water management harder. He called for better river-basin management, groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation. He also said India must move from reacting to water problems to predicting them with the help of technology. As India works towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, he said smart and sustainable water use will be key.

## Key Points

- The Vice-President launched the SURM Framework and an AI/ML-based reservoir sediment management system.
- He said 10 inter-State agreements on water sharing have been signed so far.
- He praised the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement among six States as a strong example of teamwork.
- He recalled his 19,000-km Ratha Yatra across Tamil Nadu, which spread awareness about river interlinking and water conservation.
- He said river interlinking can help when some regions face floods and others face drought.
- He supported the Prime Minister's call for “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari” and urged people to make water saving a mass movement.
- He said, “Jal Suraksha will lead to Jan Suraksha and Rashtra Suraksha.”

title: Project Rhino Started: PM Modi Marks World Rhino Day 2026
content:
What Happened

On 22 September 2026, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi marked World Rhino Day. He praised the greater one-horned rhinoceros and thanked all those working on the front lines to protect it. He shared his message in a post on X. In the same post, he announced that Project Rhino has been started.

Why It Matters

Assam is now home to nearly 80 percent of the world's rhino population. Kaziranga's work to stop rhino poaching has earned wide appreciation. Rhinos have either come back or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal. In Dudhwa, Uttar Pradesh, rhinos were brought back and that effort is creating history.

The Prime Minister said these results show the steady commitment of people to animal protection. Project Rhino will give money and technical support to range states. This help covers protection, habitat management, genetic improvement, and understanding of population dynamics. The scheme aims to take species conservation forward across the country.

Key Points

- Assam now holds nearly 80 percent of the world's rhino population.
- Kaziranga's efforts to end rhino poaching have been widely appreciated.
- Rhinos have returned or are well protected in parts of Bihar and West Bengal.
- The reintroduction of rhinos in Dudhwa, Uttar Pradesh, is creating history.
- Project Rhino will support range states with funds and technical help for protection and habitat work.
summary: On World Rhino Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the greater one-horned rhinoceros and thanked everyone protecting it. He shared that Assam is now home to nearly 80 percent of the world's rhinos. He also announced that Project Rhino has been started to help range states protect the animal and its habitat.

title: e-PAN Card: Get Your Digital PAN Free in 5-10 Minutes
content:
## What Happened

The Income Tax Department issues a digital version of your PAN card. This digital card is called e-PAN. It comes as a PDF file that you can save on your phone or computer. It has the same legal value as the plastic PAN card. So you can use it for banking, investments and tax filing.

Every e-PAN carries a QR code. That code holds your name, PAN number, date of birth and photo. Anyone can scan it to check that your card is genuine.

The government also approved the PAN 2.0 plan. About Rs 1,435 crore has been set aside for it. Under this plan, new PAN cards will carry a QR code. Your old PAN card will still work. You do not have to replace it.

## Who Is Eligible

You need three things to get a free e-PAN. You must have a valid Aadhaar number. Your mobile number must be linked to that Aadhaar, because you need it for the OTP. And you must not already have a PAN.

Some people cannot apply. Minors below 18 years cannot apply. Anyone who already has a PAN will not get a second one. If your mobile is not linked to Aadhaar, link it first at aadhaar.gov.in or at an Aadhaar centre.

## Benefits

The instant e-PAN is completely free. The department charges you nothing for it. It is generated in about 5-10 minutes. A download link lands in your email, and you can open it from anywhere.

The physical PAN card works differently. It takes 15-20 working days to reach you. You also pay a fee of about Rs 107 for it. The e-PAN is valid for your whole life. You never have to renew it. It works in almost every situation, from banks to tax filing.

## How to Apply

Step 1: Open the Income Tax e-Filing portal at incometax.gov.in.

Step 2: Click the Instant e-PAN section on the homepage.

Step 3: Choose Get New e-PAN.

Step 4: Enter your 12-digit Aadhaar number. Type only the 12 digits. Do not add dashes or spaces.

Step 5: An OTP will reach your Aadhaar-linked mobile. Verify it. If your mobile is not linked, update your Aadhaar first.

Step 6: Pick your date of birth proof from DigiLocker. You can also verify the date of birth yourself.

Step 7: Submit the form. You will get an acknowledgement number. Note it down safely.

Step 8: Within 5-10 minutes, a PDF download link reaches your email. Download it and save it.

## How to Download an Existing PAN

If you already have a PAN and want a copy, go to incometax.gov.in. Open the Reprint PAN Card section. Enter your PAN number and Aadhaar number. Pay a fee of about Rs 50. Your physical card will arrive in 15-20 working days. You can also download a digital copy from DigiLocker, which is equally valid.

## Watch Out For Scam Emails

The government has warned about fake emails going around. These emails say your PAN has expired and ask you to update it through a link. The Income Tax Department never asks for your personal details over email. Never click such links and never enter your PAN details there.

If you see a suspicious email, do not click it. Check everything only on the official portal. You can report it at webmanager@incometax.gov.in. Download the e-PAN only through official apps like mAadhaar and DigiLocker.

## Important Dates

The PAN 2.0 update was approved with a budget of Rs 1,435 crore. The year 2026 is mentioned for this plan. No exact date is given in the official source.
summary: You can now get a digital PAN card, called e-PAN, from the Income Tax Department. It is free, arrives in 5-10 minutes, and is fully valid like the physical card. The government also shared a phishing warning about fake e-PAN emails.

title: CKYC 2.0: One KYC for All Your Financial Products
content:
## What Happened

CKYC 2.0 started rolling out on August 1, 2026. CKYC stands for Central Know Your Customer. It is one central system built for India's financial sector.

Earlier, every bank, mutual fund, and insurance company did its own KYC. You had to submit the same papers again and again. Under CKYC, your details are verified once and stored in a central registry.

CERSAI manages this registry. CERSAI is the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India. It works under the RBI and is the most trusted source for KYC records.

## What Is New In CKYC 2.0

- OTP-based consent: You no longer need to hand over physical documents. One OTP is enough to give your consent.
- 14-digit CKYC identifier: This is a unique number given to you. Share it to onboard with any financial product.
- Confidence score: Every KYC record gets a score that shows how verified it is.
- Digital-first approach: Everything moves online, so paperwork drops.

## Who Can Get CKYC

Any person who wants a CKYC record must go through a regulated financial institution. Banks, mutual fund companies, and insurance companies can all do this for you. You cannot create the record on your own.

## Benefits

- You do not submit the same documents again and again. Do KYC once and use it everywhere.
- Opening a new account or investment becomes faster.
- One record covers all your financial products, including bank, mutual fund, and insurance.
- Your record sits in one secure central place.
- A central system lowers the risk of fraud.

## CKYC vs eKYC vs Normal KYC

- CKYC: Your data is stored in CERSAI's registry. Any financial institution can access it only after taking your permission.
- eKYC: This is Aadhaar-based digital verification. It happens in real time when you apply for a financial product.
- Normal KYC: You carry physical papers like PAN, Aadhaar, and address proof to the institution. They check the papers and keep the record.

## How to Register

1. Visit any regulated financial institution, such as a bank, mutual fund, or insurance company.
2. Submit the needed documents like PAN, Aadhaar, and a photo.
3. The institution verifies them and uploads them to CERSAI.
4. You receive a 14-digit CKYC identifier.
5. Use this number for fast onboarding at any other financial institution.

## How to Check Your CKYC Status

1. Open the CERSAI website at cersai.org.in.
2. Go to the CKYC Status Check section.
3. Enter your 14-digit CKYC number or your PAN number.
4. Your status will show on the screen.

If you did CKYC earlier and forgot your number, contact your bank or financial institution. They can share your CKYC number with you.
summary: CKYC 2.0 started rolling out on August 1, 2026. It lets you verify your KYC once and use the same record across banks, mutual funds, and insurance companies. The system is run by CERSAI, which works under the RBI.
